question.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=\frac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{x-3}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{x-3}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{y-3}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{y-3} \\ \sqrt[3]{y-3} & =3x \\ {(\sqrt[3]{y-3})}^{3} & ={(3x)}^{3} \\ y-3 & =27{x}^{3} \\ y & =27{x}^{3}+3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=27{x}^{3}+3.
$$
